acip: DE NAS (CIG CHAR) DU (BYUNG NAS) DE RNAMS RIM PA BZHIN DU SGRUB PA PO (BDAG NYID KYI) SPYI BO MGRIN PA SNYING GA'I (GNAS GSUM) DU SNGA PHYI (RIM) CHAR (DANG,) DE NAS (CIG CHAR) DU (THIM PA) NAS THUN MONG BA LTAR NA SROG GCOD SOGS LUS KYI SGRIB PA DANG, RDZUN DU SMRA BA SOGS NGAG GI SGRIB PA DANG, BRNAB SEMS SOGS YID KYI SGRIB PA DANG, SGO GSUM THUN MONG GI SGRIB PA STE (SGRIB) PA (BZHI DAG CING,)
wylie: de nas (cig char) du (byung nas) de rnams rim pa bzhin du sgrub pa po (bdag nyid kyi) spyi bo mgrin pa snying ga'i (gnas gsum) du snga phyi (rim) char (dang,) de nas (cig char) du (thim pa) nas thun mong ba ltar na srog gcod sogs lus kyi sgrib pa dang, rdzun du smra ba sogs ngag gi sgrib pa dang, brnab sems sogs yid kyi sgrib pa dang, sgo gsum thun mong gi sgrib pa ste (sgrib) pa (bzhi dag cing,)
english: And then they come as one, sinking into my body; into the same three places on me, the practitioner; that is, into the tip of the head, the throat, and the heart.  First they come one after the other, and then they come as one.  Relative to the shared teachings, these rays of light clean us of the four kinds of obstacles: obstacles relating to our actions (deeds such as the taking of life); obstacles relating to our speech (things like telling lies); and obstacles relating to our thoughts (such as being unhappy when others get something)--along with obstacles that involve all three of these doors of expression.
